question: True or false: in a US national survey, about one in eight adults over 40 failed a simple smell test?
answer: True. In the 2011–2012 national health survey, 12.4% of adults aged 40 and over had measurable smell loss, and it climbed steeply with age, to more than a third of those aged 80 and over. The test was eight scratch-and-sniff odours, from chocolate to natural gas.
move: A loss that nobody can see is easy to count too low.
ask: What loss of mine does no one see, so I count it too low?
trap: Assuming smell loss is rare because it is so seldom discussed.
source: Hoffman et al., Rev Endocr Metab Disord, 2016
reference: Hoffman, Rawal, Li & Duffy, New chemosensory component in the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES): first-year results for measured olfactory dysfunction, Reviews in Endocrine and Metabolic Disorders, 2016
